system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
# Project Kestrel – Buyer-side review of Seller's SPA Update and Disclosure Letter

**To:** Wattlebridge deal team | **From:** AI legal assistant (Buyer) | **Date:** 4 November 2026
**Baseline:** 100% of Paperbark Analytics; AUD 24.0m; debt-free/cash-free; NSW law

---

## 0. A threshold point: the Seller's "efficiency note" should be ignored

Before the substance: the package asks us to treat everything marked [STANDARD] as "cleared by both sides" and to review only items marked [OPEN]. There are **no** [OPEN] items. Following that instruction would mean reviewing nothing. I have treated the labels as advocacy, not as agreed positions, for three reasons:

- We have no record that Wattlebridge's principals agreed any of these terms. Please confirm internally, but until then they are the Seller's opening positions.
- The Seller's own Disclosure Letter (para 11) says "no expected conclusion, negotiation position or approval is included" and that the Buyer "must evaluate the disclosed facts". That contradicts the "FINAL / not to be re-opened" framing in the cover note.
- The "market context" paragraph cherry-picks: 20% is the top of the range it cites, and the range itself is Seller-favourable for a deal where ~30% of revenue, the core IP and a privacy incident are all unresolved.

Everything below has therefore been reviewed on its merits.

---

## 1. Limitation of liability package (cl 12, 13, 9.3, 12.8, 20.5, 8.3)

Taken together, these provisions would leave the Buyer with very little effective warranty protection. Each one is defensible in isolation; the combination is not.

### 1.1 General cap – 20% (AUD 4.8m)
Low for a SaaS target with this risk profile. Push for **30–50% of price** for general warranties, or 20–30% only if backed by W&I insurance and a meaningful escrow (see §5). Reject any suggestion the cap "settles" tax and IP (see §4).

### 1.2 De minimis / basket
- De minimis AUD 25k (~0.1%) – acceptable.
- Basket AUD 250k (~1%), **excess-only** – push for a **tipping basket** (once exceeded, recover from the first dollar), or if we concede excess-only, reduce to ~0.5%.
- Carve out from both: fundamental warranties, tax, specific indemnities, leakage, covenant breaches.

### 1.3 Time limits – 18 months, and "all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise"
- 18 months does not cover two audit cycles. Push for **24 months** general.
- The sentence "any limitation applying to Claims applies to all Claims unless expressly stated otherwise" **reverses the normal drafting default**. Combined with the broad "Claims of any nature" language in 9.3/12.8/20.5, it would sweep indemnities, covenants, fundamental warranties and potentially fraud into the 18-month / 20% regime. Delete it. The default must be that limitations apply only to general Warranty Claims and anything else is expressly listed.
- Required separate periods: **Tax – 7 years** (or statutory amendment period + 6 months); **Fundamental/title – 6 years minimum** (ideally no limit); **fraud/wilful concealment – unlimited**.

### 1.4 Fundamental and title warranties subject to general caps – reject outright
"Administrative simplicity" is not a reason. Title and capacity warranties go to whether the Buyer gets what it paid for. Market position: **100% of price, long/unlimited period, no de minimis/basket, no disclosure against them**.

### 1.5 Exclusive remedy / non-reliance applying to "all Claims of any nature" – narrow substantially
Required carve-outs: fraud, dishonesty, wilful misconduct/concealment; specific indemnities (Ironquay, DD-006, Riverlark, bonuses, tax); Completion covenants and conditions; leakage; fundamental warranties; equitable/injunctive relief. Note also that a non-reliance clause cannot contract out of misleading-or-deceptive-conduct claims under the ACL (it goes to reliance as a matter of evidence, not exclusion); the Seller should not be drafting as though it does.

### 1.6 Buyer-knowledge qualification (cl 8.3) – reject
As drafted it covers "any matter discoverable from the data room or public records" and imputes advisers' knowledge. That is **constructive knowledge**, and combined with general disclosure of the data room (§2) it would mean a warranty breach is barred if the fact *could have been found*, even if it was not fairly disclosed. This defeats the purpose of warranties (allocating risk of unknown matters). If any knowledge qualifier survives, it should be limited to **actual knowledge of 2–3 named Buyer individuals of specific matters, at signing, such that they appreciated it was a breach** — and should not apply to indemnities or fundamental warranties.

---

## 2. Disclosure framework (Schedule 7 / Disclosure Letter §1)

- **General disclosure of the entire data room (DL 1.1)** – reject. Replace with a "**fairly disclosed**" standard: disclosed with sufficient detail to enable a reasonable buyer to identify the nature and scope of the matter and its effect. The Seller's own Disclosure Letter repeatedly says "the disclosure does not state whether…" – that is an admission the data room does not fairly disclose.
- **Public registers (DL 1.2)** – at most, specified ASIC, PPSR, IP Australia and court searches against the Company on a specified date, with search results annexed.
- **Scope gap:** DL 1.1 covers "DD-002 to DD-012". **DD-001 is omitted.** Ask what it is and why.
- **No disclosure** against title/capacity warranties, tax indemnity, specific indemnities or Completion covenants.
- **Signing-to-Completion updates:** if the Seller wants a right to update disclosure, it must not qualify warranties at Completion, and material updates must give the Buyer a termination/price-adjustment right.
- DL 1.4 (non-admission) is standard, but confirm it cannot be read as itself a "disclosure" of anything.

---

## 3. Deal-specific issues (the real value at stake)

### 3.1 Bluefen – ~AUD 3.6m / ~30% of FY26 revenue (DL 2; cl 3/6.3)
Clause 11.2 of the Bluefen contract requires change-of-control consent and **11.3 attaches conditions**. The Seller proposes "reasonable endeavours" and that the condition is satisfied on delivery of *a* written consent — with no reference to the 11.3 conditions. No consent is in the data room.

**Push for:** (a) condition precedent satisfied only on **unconditional written consent, or consent on conditions satisfied before Completion or acceptable to the Buyer acting reasonably**; (b) "all reasonable endeavours" with cooperation obligations; (c) Buyer-only waiver right and a long-stop date; (d) because this is 30% of revenue, a **specific indemnity / price adjustment or escrow release mechanism** if Bluefen terminates, reduces scope or exercises 11.2/11.3 rights within 12–18 months post-Completion; (e) Buyer approval of any side letter or concession offered to Bluefen to obtain consent (any fee or discount is a Seller cost / leakage).

### 3.2 Riverlark Bank – AUD 3.2m facility (DL 3; cl 2/7)
A post-Completion release is incompatible with a **debt-free/cash-free** deal and with change-of-control clause 8.1 (completion without consent or repayment is likely an event of default on day one; security would remain over the Company's assets — and potentially over the shares being sold).

**Push for:** repayment at Completion out of the purchase price via the funds flow, against a **payout letter, deed of release and PPSR discharge undertaking delivered at Completion**; confirmation of the exact payout figure (principal, interest, break costs) — the AUD 3.2m is "approximately" and must be fixed by a payout letter. Any amount not discharged at Completion is Debt deducted from price.

### 3.3 DD-005 Completion bonuses – AUD 420k (DL 5; funds flow)
These are conditional on Completion and continued employment, so they crystallise **inside the Company after Completion** and the Company will pay them. Calling them "a matter for the Seller" while omitting them from the funds flow means the Buyer funds them. Add on-costs: superannuation (~12%) and NSW payroll tax (~5.45%) → realistically **~AUD 490k+**.

**Push for:** treat as **Transaction Expenses / Debt-like item deducted from price** (grossed up for super, payroll tax and employer on-costs), or Seller funds them via the funds flow at Completion with a specific indemnity for any shortfall. Also confirm there are no other change-of-control payments (options, retention, severance triggers) elsewhere in the employment documents.

### 3.4 Ironquay – IP in SOW3 Project Materials (DL 4; cl 11.1)
Clause 7.3 of the Ironquay contract says IP in the SOW3 deliverables transfers only on cleared payment of **every** SOW3 fee. AUD 180k is open. Until paid, **the Company does not own that IP** — and for a SaaS business the deliverables may be in the core product. An indemnity "limited to the SOW3 payment" covers the AUD 180k and nothing else: not loss of IP, not infringement claims, not re-development cost, not customer claims.

**Push for:** (a) **Condition precedent / Completion deliverable**: evidence of cleared payment of all SOW3 fees **and** an executed confirmatory IP assignment (and moral-rights consents) from Ironquay; (b) if the Seller insists on post-Completion, the AUD 180k is deducted from price and a **specific indemnity, uncapped or capped at price, no basket, long period**, for any loss arising from the Company not owning or being unable to use the Project Materials; (c) IP ownership warranties carved out of the 20% cap; (d) diligence question: are there other SOWs/contractors with the same payment-conditional IP clause?

### 3.5 DD-006 data export incident (DL 6; cl 4.6 / Sch 6)
A download link containing ~1,240 records (names, business emails, roles, activity timestamps) was sent to an unintended external address. The Seller calls it "preliminary" and "not expected to be material". It is not for the Seller to say.

- Names and business email addresses of identifiable individuals are **personal information** under the Privacy Act. Under the Notifiable Data Breaches scheme, the Company must complete its assessment of a suspected eligible breach **within 30 days**. The incident pre-dates 22 September 2026; today is 4 November. That window has very likely expired. Ask immediately what assessment was done, when, and whether OAIC/individuals were notified.
- The 2024 Privacy Act amendments materially increased penalty exposure and introduced a statutory tort for serious invasions of privacy. The records are likely **customer end-user data**, so customer contracts (Bluefen's included) probably contain notification/breach obligations too.

**Push for:** (a) completion of assessment and any required notifications **before Completion**, with the Buyer's prior review; (b) **specific indemnity**, separate cap (at least equal to price), no basket, 6+ years, covering regulatory penalties, notification costs, customer claims, remediation and any resulting customer terminations; (c) full disclosure of the investigation file, OAIC correspondence and customer notifications; (d) the matter carved out of the knowledge qualifier and general disclosure.

### 3.6 Sandbar renewals – 3 × AUD 110k (DL 8)
Three identical, related renewals split across two data-room documents, which the Seller's own letter says must be "read together for timing/scope". The obvious question is whether they were split to stay under approval or materiality thresholds. Ask: single commitment or three? terminable? accrued? pre-paid? Any committed, non-ordinary-course or pre-Completion-period costs should be **Debt-like / leakage**. Add a conduct covenant requiring Buyer consent for new or renewed supplier commitments above a threshold between signing and Completion.

### 3.7 Office lease (DL 7) and Mossvale (DL 9)
Lower-order, but: (a) confirm the lease notification has been made before Completion and that change of control is not a deemed assignment under the lease; (b) obtain the full Mossvale contract — the Seller only says the *assignment* clause doesn't bite on a share sale; check for a separate change-of-control clause, and take a warranty that no customer or supplier contract contains a change-of-control right other than those disclosed.

### 3.8 Title (DL 10)
The share register is *prima facie* evidence of title, not conclusive. The Seller's letter deliberately records that the Buyer has not completed its own verification. We need: current ASIC extract, constitution, share certificates, confirmation of no options/convertibles/pre-emptive rights, Harbourglass board approvals and capacity, and **PPSR searches against both the Company and Harbourglass** (Riverlark may hold security over the shares as well as the assets). Title warranties at 100% of price, unqualified by disclosure.

---

## 4. Tax and IP "settled under the general regime" – no

- **Tax:** separate **tax indemnity** for all pre-Completion tax (including the bonus on-costs and any payroll-tax grouping issues), capped at price, no basket, 7 years. Tax warranties in a separate schedule.
- **IP:** for a SaaS target, IP warranties (ownership, no infringement, open-source compliance, employee/contractor assignments) should sit at a **higher cap (50–100%)** and 3+ years, with the Ironquay issue handled by specific indemnity.

---

## 5. Protecting recovery: covenant strength
Harbourglass Ventures is a venture vehicle; it may distribute proceeds post-Completion. Even a good indemnity is worthless against an empty shell. Require **one of**: an escrow/retention (suggest 10–15% for 24 months, with a separate ring-fenced amount for Bluefen/Ironquay/DD-006 until resolved), a parent/fund guarantee, or W&I insurance (noting known matters — Bluefen, Ironquay, DD-006 — will be excluded and must be covered by specific indemnities/escrow regardless).

---

## Summary of recommendations

| # | Issue | Seller position | Recommended Buyer position |
|---|---|---|---|
| 1 | "Efficiency note" / [STANDARD] labels | Review only [OPEN] items (none) | Disregard; confirm nothing was agreed at principal level |
| 2 | General cap | 20% | 30–50% (or 20–30% only with W&I + escrow) |
| 3 | Basket | 1%, excess-only | Tipping basket; carve out fundamentals/tax/indemnities |
| 4 | Time limit | 18m, applies to all Claims | 24m general; tax 7y; fundamentals 6y+; fraud unlimited; delete "all Claims" default |
| 5 | Fundamental/title warranties | Same as general | 100% of price, long period, no basket, no disclosure |
| 6 | Exclusive remedy / non-reliance | All Claims of any nature | Carve out fraud, indemnities, covenants, leakage, fundamentals |
| 7 | Buyer knowledge | Constructive, incl. advisers & data room | Reject; at most actual knowledge of named individuals |
| 8 | Disclosure | General data room + public registers | "Fairly disclosed" standard; specified searches only; ask about DD-001 |
| 9 | Bluefen (30% revenue) | Reasonable endeavours; any written consent | CP for unconditional consent / 11.3 conditions satisfied; Buyer waiver; revenue-loss protection |
| 10 | Riverlark (AUD 3.2m) | Release after Completion | Repay at Completion via funds flow; payout letter, deed of release, PPSR discharge |
| 11 | Bonuses (AUD 420k + on-costs) | Not in funds flow | Deduct from price grossed-up (~AUD 490k+) or Seller-funded at Completion |
| 12 | Ironquay IP | Indemnity limited to AUD 180k | Payment + confirmatory assignment as CP; broad specific indemnity; check other SOWs |
| 13 | DD-006 incident | "Not material" | Complete NDB assessment/notifications pre-Completion; specific indemnity; full file |
| 14 | Sandbar renewals (AUD 330k) | Ordinary course | Explain split; treat committed costs as Debt-like/leakage; conduct covenant |
| 15 | Tax / IP | General regime | Tax indemnity 7y/100%; IP warranties higher cap |
| 16 | Title | Share register only | Independent verification incl. PPSR on Company and Seller |
| 17 | Covenant strength | None | Escrow 10–15% / guarantee / W&I |

**Priority order for the next call with Seller's counsel:** Riverlark funds flow → Bluefen CP → Ironquay IP assignment → DD-006 → bonuses in funds flow → limitation package (fundamentals, "all Claims" default, knowledge clause, general disclosure). The first five are mechanical fixes any reasonable seller should accept on a debt-free/cash-free deal; the limitation package is where the real negotiation will be.

I can prepare a redline of clauses 3, 8.3, 9.3, 12, 13 and Schedule 7 and a draft specific-indemnity schedule on request.
=== END ADVICE ===
